verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents its reviews as 'context-aware'. It applies repository conventions automatically through detected guideline files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules) and learned team preferences. Its multi-repo analysis detects breaking changes, API mismatches, and dependency issues across linked repositories, which goes beyond the changed hunks. However, the evidence never explicitly says that in-repo reviews analyze call sites or related modules of the same repository, so the core 'whole-repo' claim rests on vague marketing language. Missing for 10: explicit docs that PR reviews trace in-repo call sites and related modules, and independent or hands-on corroboration that comments reflect repo-wide context.
